newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch food industry approves gene-altered soy.
newsitem.headline: Dutch food industry approves gene-altered soy.

text.p: The Dutch Food and Drink Industry Association said on Tuesday its members would be using new genetically-altered soya, pitting them against environmental groups, who have vowed to keep up an anti-import campaign.

"This month, soybeans will be imported into the Netherlands which have been produced with the help of modern bio-technology. The Dutch food sector only processes and sells products that are safe for the consumer and which have government approval," the Nederlandse Voedingsmiddelen Industrie said in a statement.
It said health authorities in the United States, UK, European Union, Canada and Japan had also approved the product.

Greenpeace this week has written to the main supermarket chains in the country, saying the new beans "offered the consumer no advantage and were nothing more than a worldwide experiment with our food and environment."
Other environmental groups have joined the protest, calling on Dutch-based food giants such as Unilever to halt using them.
"Our campaign of direct action will continue," a spokesman for Amsterdam-based Greenpeace International said.

The first vessel, the Ideal Progress, carrying the new beans -- developed by U.S. chemicals firm Monsanto -- is due to dock in Hamburg late on Tuesday evening, paradoxically in the European country where consumer fears have been the greatest.
Some German firms, including the German arm of Unilever, have said public pressure there has been so great that they will not be using the soybeans.

But the Dutch Food and Drink Association said it believed that informing the consumer was the way forward. It said that as it believed separating normal beans from the new type was very difficult a widespread information campaign was needed.
It said there was a free telephone number to take consumer calls and brochures giving background information.
